pr_title: Add overloads for problem and validation problem results that accept `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<,>>`

- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

## Description

This PRs add overloads for problem and validation problem results that accept `IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<,>>`.

For the moment I'm not sure to understand why I get the warning `RS0026 Symbol 'ValidationProblem' violates the backcompat requirement: 'Do not add multiple overloads with optional parameters'`, so I'm open to suggestions.

Fixes #41899.
Fixes #56370.

I think we're going to want to suppress this warning. Even though this overload is more permissive and accepts all the same parameters as the other equal-length overload, it's still getting flagged by the analyzer because it doesn't have the "most parameters amongst its public overloads".

```csharp
#pragma warning disable RS0027 // Public API with optional parameter(s) should have the most parameters amongst its public overloads
public static IResult Problem(
        string? detail = null,
        string? instance = null,
        int? statusCode = null,
        string? title = null,
        string? type = null,
        IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, object?>>? extensions = null)
#pragma warning restore RS0027 // Public API with optional parameter(s) should have the most parameters amongst its public overloads
```

Unless someone like @jaredpar or @CyrusNajmabadi can explain why this is a terrible idea. See https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/41899#issuecomment-1476727981 if you need more context.

TBH I don't recall the exact problem this is preventing. This warning falls under the "back compat" blanket so it's likely trying to prevent a situation where you add a new overload and it silently changes the binding of existing source code. Possible I'm just not creative enough right now to think of a scenario. 

These rules were written originally in the context of Roslyn. It's possible this was more specific to the way we did them. 

Possible @333fred understands the problem this is preventing.
I'm not sure either. FWIW, this is a commonly-disabled rule in roslyn.
Thank you for your feedback. I disabled the rule.
Can you elaborate a bit on why you preferred to have two separate code paths, rather than having the new overload delegate to the old one?  I can see arguments in both directions.

This method just delegates to `TypedResult`. In `TypedResult`, if I do `return Problem(detail, instance, statusCode, title, type, extensions);` to call the other overload, it calls the same method and creates a recursion.
You should be able to force a particular overload with casting.
(Not recommending you do that, just saying it doesn't seem like a compelling reason one way or the other on its own.)
I avoided duplicating using a cast.
